questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To chose a city that I could see myself have a normal everyday life and get to know the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Our Erasmus person in milan was very good at introducing us to the city when we first got there, and also the information given by Erasmus about events was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Medium. I would recommend looking at Facebook groups and also search up rentals in milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: One of the campus is pretty far away from the school, so if you enjoy being nearby the city and not having to pay that much for transportation it is a good idea to look for an apartment yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you have to apply for the school and get accepted, when this is done it is fairly easy to accept the spot. You have a lot of time to chose which courses you would like to attend, and also have the opportunity to try a few different ones in the first weeks to make up your mind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors are also very helpful at answering questions you might have. And also Massimo Costa was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, all my classes were accepted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find housing as soon as possible and try to stay inside the next biggest circle around the city, as it is not easy to get a bike and public transportation is almost the same amount of time as walking.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very different. Some of the courses like "Game Theory" and "Business History" was fairly easy, whereas the courses "Risk Management" and "Causal inference and policy evaluation" was a completely different level and hard to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different in the way that some of the courses offer two different exams, depending on whether you attend a certain percent of the classes. Eg. if you attend 70% there is a take home exam where you have to submit an assignment, or else it is a closed book exam at the campus. Also the courses and the professors use presentations a lot more than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Game theory, Business History, Causal inference and policy evaluation, Corporate finance and Risk management.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Game theory I would recommend due to the professor whom was good at giving examples of how the exam would look like and providing task to study for the exam. The exam was also manageable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to want to travel across italy, where the train tickets and cost of living are not the worst but still a considerable cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating at restaurants are cheaper than in Denmark, but still Milan is one of the most expensive cities in italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure, but didn't feel as available as you could have hoped.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't take part in any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips to other cities like Como, cinque terre, bologna, pisa, rome. It is pretty cheap to rent a car if you are more people and then it is nice to see some different cities. Just be aware of the zones in the bigger cities about payment.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The city is pretty international and most of the people speak English. If you want to make italian friends you have to make an effort and don't expect them to talk to you in class.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of eating at restaurants and just being out of the house a lot of the time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: There are going to be a lot of fellow danish exchange students in milan, so if you want to meet foreigners you should be aware of this. But if you want to get good danish friends and make great memories this is possible. Try to attend as much as the classes as you can, as the exams are designed for you to attend and it is harder to study for it at home before the exam.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to enjoy the city as much as you can by finding small little favorite places, as this is also a high paced city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of fellow exchange student and living in a little bubble and experiencing the city. Also if you like running, you should attend a halffmarathon

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being occupied with exiting stuff while studying for exams while being on your own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
